text: DreamBooth adapts pretrained text-to-image diffusion models from three to five subject images to preserve identity while changing context and appearance. Fine-tuning pairs a rare-token identifier with the subject's class, linking instance learning to pretrained class knowledge. A prior-preservation loss uses class images generated by the frozen model to counter the tendency to replace the class with the learned instance. We provide a public 30-subject dataset and evaluation protocol, proposing DINO embedding similarity to assess subject identity alongside prompt alignment. Across 3,000 generated images, DreamBooth on Stable Diffusion improves DINO similarity from 0.569 to 0.668 and CLIP text-image similarity from 0.255 to 0.305 over Textual Inversion. User preferences likewise favor DreamBooth for identity (68% versus 22%) and prompt fidelity (81% versus 12%): these joint comparisons support retaining the subject while following changed prompts. An Imagen ablation finds less class collapse and greater diversity with prior preservation, but slightly lower subject fidelity. Applications include novel viewpoints, artistic renditions, and property changes; rare contexts, context-appearance entanglement, overfitting, and hallucinated details still limit preservation.

Toolformer learns when and how to invoke external APIs from feedback on whether their responses improve continuation prediction. A few demonstrations per text-based API guide candidate calls; executed calls survive only if their results lower next-token loss relative to both no call and a call without its result. Fine-tuning GPT-J on these augmented texts turns predictive utility into supervision for tool selection and use, without downstream-task demonstrations. In prompted zero-shot evaluations permitting at most one call with call-encouraging decoding, Toolformer improves factual completion, arithmetic, question answering, and temporal tasks over GPT-J baselines. On ASDiv, first-number accuracy is 40.4% with calls enabled versus 14.8% with calls disabled, indicating that inference-time access adds benefit beyond tool-annotated training. We introduce the template-generated DATESET benchmark, where calendar access supplies useful temporal context. Search-assisted question answering remains below GPT-3; translation helps the tool-trained model across languages but does not consistently beat original GPT-J. With calls disabled, perplexity matches content-matched fine-tuning without API annotations. In three-tool scaling tests, most benefits emerge around 775M parameters, with search an exception. Independently generated training calls do not teach chained or interactive tool use.

Toolformer learns tool-use decisions through self-supervised language modeling, using a few demonstrations per tool. Candidate calls are executed and retained when their responses improve subsequent token prediction over both no-call and call-only alternatives; fine-tuning on augmented text teaches tool selection, argument generation, and response incorporation. Experiments use GPT-J and five text-based APIs in prompted zero-shot evaluation with at most one call per input. On ASDiv, accuracy is 40.4%, versus 9.6% after fine-tuning on the same text without calls and 14.8% with Toolformer's calls disabled, supporting useful tool access beyond further training alone. This exceeds GPT-3 (175B) at 14.0%, whereas question answering improves over GPT-J controls but remains below GPT-3. Factual completion and temporal benchmarks improve; translation calls help across evaluated languages without consistently surpassing unmodified GPT-J. With calls disabled, perplexity matches text-only fine-tuning on both evaluated corpora. In a three-tool GPT-2 sweep, useful tool use appears near 775M parameters, with search an exception; stronger base models can diminish weaker tools' utility. Independent call generation leaves chained and interactive use unsupported, limiting the evidence to noninteractive tool access.

DreamBooth personalizes a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model from three to five images so that a specific subject can appear in new, text-specified settings. Pairing a rare-token identifier with the subject's class connects the new identity to existing class knowledge; a prior-preservation loss on class images generated by the original model counteracts collapse of the class onto that identity. We release an evaluation suite of 30 subjects and 25 prompts per subject and introduce a DINO-based subject-fidelity metric. On Stable Diffusion, DreamBooth improves DINO similarity from 0.569 to 0.668 and text-image CLIP similarity from 0.255 to 0.305 relative to Textual Inversion. Improvement on both measures supports identity retention alongside prompt-directed variation, rather than resemblance alone. Majority-vote human preferences favor DreamBooth at 68% for subject fidelity and 81% for prompt fidelity. Imagen ablations show that prior preservation reduces class collapse and increases diversity, but slightly lowers subject fidelity. Qualitative examples extend to artistic renditions, novel viewpoints, and property modifications, although context-appearance entanglement, overfitting, and hallucinated details constrain identity preservation.
